question: How far does Europa orbit from Jupiter, and what is the one-way light delay from Earth to Europa at 628 million km?

draft.answer: Europa’s average orbital distance from Jupiter is about 671,000 km (417,000 miles). At an Earth–Europa distance of 628 million km, the one-way light delay is about 2,094.8 seconds, or 34.9 minutes, assuming light travels through vacuum in a straight line.
draft.why: The orbital distance is documented by NASA/JPL, and the signal delay is computed for the stated distance under the calculator’s assumptions.

claims.text: Europa orbits Jupiter at an average distance of about 671,000 km (417,000 miles).

sources.title: Quick Facts | NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)
sources.quote: Europa orbits Jupiter relatively quickly, circling the planet every 3.55 Earth days at a distance of about 417,000 miles (671,000 kilometers) from the planet — roughly 1.75 times farther than our own Moon is to Earth.

claims.text: At 628,000,000 km, the one-way light delay is 2,094.8 seconds, or 34.913 minutes, assuming a straight path through vacuum.
